svg.title: Hallucination Cases: perception error and reasoning drift
svg.desc: Editable reconstruction of a two-row explanatory figure. Base frames divide each row into User Input, Head, Visual Attention, Textual Attention, and Head-level Contribution. Row 1 contains a no-left-turn style visual prompt, dominant/better perception heads, visual-attention grids, token-attention tables, and a contribution heatmap. Row 2 contains an airplane-in-sky prompt, dominant/better reasoning heads, visual-attention grids, token-attention tables, and a second contribution heatmap. Objects are positioned relative to each row's left-origin and separated by dashed vertical section dividers.

g.desc: Origin is the no-left-turn sign frame at upper left. The prompt text is directly below it. The sign consists of a white square border, red prohibition circle/slash, black left-turn arrow with vertical stem and right-pointing top segment.
Dominating Head is above Better Perception Head. Each rounded head label is anchored to a small colored robot head icon at its upper-left corner; bullet layer/head descriptors are below each box.

The top grid has sparse pale red activations and is labeled Less Visual Attention. The lower grid has a small dark green sign-like activation and is labeled More Visual Attention. Both grids are square and vertically stacked.

Textual attention is a stack of token rows with dashed separators. The origin row begins at Visual tokens and moves rightward across token cells. Dominating perception table emphasizes visual/sign tokens; generation row points to the hallucinated token no while the reference yes is below-right.

Contribution heatmap at right has pale blue gridded matrix, axis labels, and two callout boxes. A red outlined high contribution cell near top center is linked to a red label; a better-perception low contribution region near left-middle is linked to a blue label.
Origin is the airplane picture frame under the case title. The drawing depicts a small aircraft banking through blue sky and clouds. The yes/no question text sits below the picture.
Dominating Head and Better Reasoning Head are vertically arranged like row one. The dominant head is layer 27 head 26; the better reasoning head is layer 27 head 21.
Top grid for row two has pale red scattered visual activations and is labeled More Visual Attention. Lower grid is mostly blank and labeled Less Visual Attention.

Row two token table emphasizes reasoning tokens. The blue attention row has strong entries around aircraft, typically, windows, and not. A green arrow from reasoning-related tokens points to the correct not token, while the generated answer still shows no with a red cross and Reference Yes.

Second contribution heatmap has pale blue matrix with strong cells at lower-right, red callout for High Contribution Dominating Head and blue callout for Low Contribution Better Reasoning Head. Arrows connect boxes to cells.
